newsitem.title: RUSSIA: AGROKHLEB - Russia '97 winter grain crop seen flat.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB - Russia '97 winter grain crop seen flat.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from the Agrokhleb Report, published by SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union.
DESPITE DECLINE IN CURRENT WINTER GRAIN PLANTINGS, 1997 WINTER GRAIN OUTPUT MAY REMAIN AT 1996 LEVEL
MOSCOW, Nov 20 - Winter grain plantings and autumn ploughing have started with delays across Russia (Table 1).
Delayed completion of the 1996 harvest, especially in the Urals and Western Siberian regions, is partly responsible for the delays.
In the Northern Caucasus, which usually produces about 50 percent of Russia's total winter wheat crop, early winter crop development was affected by dry weather in September.
In addition, farmers there are experiencing troubles with fuel supplies for autumn fieldwork.
As a result, the total area sown to winter crops for the 1996 harvest is expected to be 14.0-14.5 million hectares, about one million ha down on last year.
However, rainy and unusually warm weather in October has somewhat improved crop development in the European part of Russia.
Moreover, sowing of winter grain crops in the Northern Caucasus was underway by mid-November and the region is likely to maintain winter grain plantings at last year's level of 4.3 million hectares.
Assuming average yields, winter grain output in 1997 may remain close to the 1996 level of 27 million tonnes.
